title: Compact mosaic token system and dynamic rollout affordances for cost microcards
creator: Aisha Moretti
description:
Summary:
Design and prototype a compact 'mosaic' token system targeted at cost microcards and rollout state affordances across the Redwood Console. This ticket delivers a constrained token palette, component variants, and an interactive Figma pattern lab that demonstrates responsive behaviors (XS to L), density toggles, and rollout states (canary, stable, draining, fallback). The goal is to reduce visual entropy in dense dashboard surfaces while preserving affordances needed for rollout controls and quick cost inspection.

Context and motivation:
- Multiple console screens show high-density cost tiles and rollout rails where current tokens are inconsistent across teams. This leads to spacing mismatches, inconsistent emphasis on status pills, and visual noise when many cards are present.
- Engineering needs a compact, predictable set of tokens (spacing, elevation, type scale, color ramps) that maps cleanly to dedicated and hosted product views so runtime-sensitive dashboards remain legible at high card counts.
- Product wants clear, scannable rollout states with a small surface footprint for PLG onboarding and for power users monitoring Live rollouts.

Deliverables:
1) Token palette (names, intended usage, and aliasing rules) for compact surfaces: spacing, radii, elevation, type scales, iconography sizes, and micro-interaction durations.
2) Component variants for Microcard (3 density sizes), Rollout-Pill (4 states), and CardHeader (compact title + meta area).
3) Figma pattern lab prototype with interactive variants + copyable token tokens; includes a density toggle and simulated data sets to validate legibility at 6, 12, and 24 cards per row.
4) Accessibility validations (contrast checks, keyboard focus states, reduced-motion variants).
5) Handoff notes for engineering: token mapping table, CSS/JSON export, and example usage patterns for cost sparkline, small avatar stacks, and quick- actions overflow.

Constraints and trade-offs considered:
- We prioritize a single compact token set over infinite flexibility to reduce fragmentation across console pages. That increases initial cognitive load (narrower choices) but reduces long-term maintenance.
- Tightening vertical rhythm risks truncation of long titles; we include rules to allow title wrapping at 2 lines with ellipsis policy and a tooltip for full content.
- Micro-interactions are simplified (fewer different durations) to avoid animation jitter at scale; however we provide a reduced-motion variant for accessibility.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Figma prototype demonstrates all variants and density toggles, and is annotated with token names and use cases.
- Design checklist and token mapping table are attached and reviewed by at least one PM and one ENG owner.
- Automated contrast report (screenshot + tool output) included showing WCAG AA compliance for primary card states.
- Engineering has a clear mapping doc (JSON + CSS variables) and a sample React story demonstrating microcards with rollout states and density control.

2026-03-04 - Eng feedback (Samir Patel): Asked for explicit token names that map to existing runtime classes; requested a JSON export for rapid import into the design tokens repo.
2026-03-08 - Accessibility review (Maya Johnson): Noted contrast issue for 'draining' pill at small sizes — suggested a darker ramp or outline. Marked as resolved in prototype.
2026-03-10 - Design critique (internal): Align on 8px baseline grid for horizontal spacing and a 4px micro-step for vertical compressions; Rafael to finalize spacing table.
2026-03-11 - Final review (Rafael Chen): Approved visual language; requested two additional microcard examples with dense embedding lists and long titles for edge-case testing.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype includes density toggles (XS/S/M) and simulated datasets for 6/12/24 cards to validate spacing and truncation.
Token export JSON and CSS variable file uploaded to design-tokens repo with unit mapping and a one-page usage guide.
Accessibility contrast report attached and keyboard focus states documented for all interactive elements.
At least one ENG owner (ENG-40211) and PM sign-off recorded in comments before merging tokens into main library.
